cards.title: Practice, honestly
cards.text: 463 laps run and nothing at stake. What it does tell you is who looks comfortable and who is fighting the car.

cards.title: Russell: 1:45.387
cards.text: In a Mercedes. Take practice times with salt: fuel loads are secret and nobody shows their hand.

cards.title: Albon racked up 28 laps
cards.text: Track time is the currency of a practice Thursday. Whoever runs most learns most, and burns the most rubber doing it.

cards.title: Russell had the best average over his quicker laps
cards.text: Every lap within 4% of each driver's own best, averaged. Fuel loads are unknown, so read it as a hint, not a ranking.

cards.title: What they ran, and on what
cards.text: Compound choice in practice is a rehearsal for the race plan.

cards.title: Leclerc topped the trap at 339 km/h
cards.text: Early wing choices show up here before anybody admits to them.

cards.title: Flags out 8 times
cards.text: Every interruption costs somebody a run they had planned.

cards.title: Track between 49°C and 51°C
cards.text: Practice conditions rarely match the race, which is one more reason these times mislead.
